name: sprite2d
description: Pictures for entities: a sprite is one cell of an atlas drawn at the entity's Position, and an animation steps through consecutive cells. Tiles, characters, items and effects are all sprites.

components.name: Sprite
components.description: Draws one cell of an atlas centred on the entity's Position. atlas names an atlas of the game (game.json "atlases"); frame is the cell number, counted row by row from the top left. width and height are in world units, 0 meaning the cell's own size. Sprites with a higher layer are drawn over lower ones; at equal layers the older entity is drawn first. red, green, blue and alpha (0 to 255) tint and fade the picture; 255 leaves it as it is. pivot_x and pivot_y say which point of the picture sits on the Position: 0 is the left or top edge, 0.5 the middle (the default), 1 the right or bottom edge; they need a width and a height to have an effect. With screen, the Position and the size are pixels of the window and the camera does not move or zoom the sprite: that is how an interface stays put while the world scrolls. additive adds the picture's light to what is under it (glows, sparks, rays of light: black adds nothing); multiply darkens what is under it by the picture's colour (shadows, tints: white changes nothing); with neither it simply covers what is under it. A transform2d.Rotation turns the picture around its Position. When the game has lighting (module light2d), a sprite is darkened by the dark and brightened by the lights around it; unlit keeps its own colours (a sky, a far plane painted with its own light, a glow), and light makes the picture a light instead of a drawing: it is added to the light map and brightens what is around it (a shaft of sunlight, a lit window), without being drawn itself. Without lighting, unlit changes nothing and a light sprite is not drawn. over_effects draws it in the world, but after the screen effects (postfx): never blurred nor darkened by them (the one thing kept sharp while all around is blurred, a pause).

components.name: Parallax
components.description: Makes the entity's Sprite a plane at a distance: x and y say how much of the camera's movement it follows (1 moves with the world, 0.5 half as much, as a far plane does; 0 stays put on the screen, as the sky does; above 1 moves faster, as a plane nearer than the action does). The zoom applies to it as to the rest. With repeat_x the picture is drawn again side by side, every width, across the whole view: one picture makes an endless band (hills, clouds, a ground). Put the farthest planes on the lowest layers.

components.name: SpriteAnimation
components.description: Makes the entity's Sprite play the cells first_frame, first_frame + 1, ... for frame_count cells, each shown for ticks_per_frame simulation ticks. With looping it starts over; without, it stays on the last cell. elapsed counts the ticks played and is the animation's own state: leave it at 0, or set it to start part-way.

components.name: FrameBind
components.description: Chooses the Sprite's picture from a number of the game: every tick, the entity's own number field (written "module.Component.field", for example "slide_merge.Tile.value") gives the cell first_frame + n, where n is the number itself, or its base 2 logarithm rounded down (2 gives 1, 8 gives 3, 0 gives 0) with log2. frame_count, when more than 0, stops it on the last of that many cells. The colour of a tile from its value, a gauge, a state shown by a picture. A missing component leaves n at 0.

components.name: Animator
components.description: Chooses the entity's animation from its state, among the AnimationClips of its set (an item of the game's animation_set list): every tick, the clip with the highest priority whose condition holds for this entity is played by its SpriteAnimation (one is added when it has none). Switching to another clip starts it from its first cell; staying on the same one lets it run on. Many entities can share one set: every enemy of a kind, every copy of a prefab. When it goes from one clip to another and a transition clip of the set joins them, the transition plays first, once, then the new clip (a turn between running left and running right, a landing between falling and standing). clip (the id of the clip it is on) and transition (the ticks of transition left) are kept for you.

components.name: AnimationClip
components.description: One animation of a set, for the Animators of that set: an entity of its own, which draws nothing. It plays the cells first_frame to first_frame + frame_count - 1, each for ticks_per_frame ticks, over and over with looping, or once and then stays on the last. It is chosen when its condition holds: the animated entity's own number field ("module.Component.field", for example "transform2d.Velocity.y" or "collision2d.Blocked.below", a bool counting as 0 or 1) is between min and max. With absolute the size of the number is compared, whatever its sign (a speed in either direction). A clip without a field always holds: give it the lowest priority, it is what plays when nothing else does. Among the clips that hold, the highest priority wins, then the oldest. A missing component makes the condition fail. and_field, with and_min and and_max, is a second condition that must hold too (rising and going right: a jump to the right); none, the default, adds nothing. id is a number for the clip in its set, for transitions. A clip with a from_id is a transition instead, never chosen by a condition: it plays once when an Animator of its set goes from the clip with id from_id to the clip with id to_id (to any clip when to_id is left out; a transition for that very pair wins over one to any clip). and_absolute compares the size of the second number, whatever its sign: both numbers small, a character that hardly moves (floating, drifting).

components.name: Facing
components.description: Turns the Sprite towards where the entity goes: when its number (field, "module.Component.field"; none, the default, reads the entity's transform2d.Velocity x) goes above threshold the picture faces right, below -threshold it faces left, and in between it keeps its side (a character that stops keeps looking the way it went). drawn_left says the picture itself faces left. The side is kept in the Sprite's flip_x.

systems.name: choose_clip
systems.description: Gives every Animator the clip of its set that its state asks for (see AnimationClip), with the transition that joins it to the previous one, before the animations advance.

systems.name: animate
systems.description: Advances every SpriteAnimation by one tick (by less in a slow motion, transform2d.WorldSpeed: carry keeps the share of a tick not played yet) and sets its Sprite's frame. It runs in the simulation, so an animation is the same on every run and every machine.

systems.name: face
systems.description: Turns every Sprite that has a Facing towards where its entity goes.

systems.name: draw
systems.description: Asks the renderer to draw every Sprite, lowest layer first, with the drawings other modules put on a layer (LayeredDraws, ge/mod/sprite2d/layered.hpp). Presentation only: it never changes the simulation. The frame is ended by whoever runs the loop.

systems.name: bind_frame
systems.description: Sets the frame of every Sprite that has a FrameBind from the entity's own number.
